thread.title: Lumentum Stock Falls On Huawei Worries As Oclaro Deal Approved | Investor's Business Daily

author: REINHARDT KRAUSE
title: Lumentum Stock Falls On Huawei Worries As Oclaro Deal Approved | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Lumentum Holdings ( LITE ) on Thursday said Chinese regulators have approved its $1.7 billion purchase of Oclaro ( OCLR ) amid the ongoing U.S.-China trade and technology war. Lumentum stock, though, fell as the arrest of a top executive at Huawei raised worries over its sales of optical devices to the Chinese telecom network gear maker.
X Milpitas, Calif.-based Lumentum, in a release, said China's State Administration for Market Regulation has approved the Oclaro acquisition. The deal originally was announced in March.
China's antitrust regulators did not give a green light to Qualcomm 's ( QCOM ) purchase of Europe-based chipmaker NXP Semiconductors ( NXPI ).
The lack of approval for the Qualcomm deal raised questions over the fate of Lumentum and Oclaro. Lumentum says it now expects the Oclaro purchase to close on Monday.

Please contact customer service CLOSE NeoPhotonics Stock Takes Hit Lumentum stock slipped 0.9% to close at 44.73 on the stock market today , despite approval of the Oclaro deal. NeoPhotonics ( NPTN ) stock took a much bigger hit, as Huawei is its biggest customer. NeoPhotonics stock plunged 16% to 6.49.
According to a UBS report, NeoPhotonics garners 40% of sales from Huawei. Lumentum and Oclaro each get about 11% of sales from Huawei, or nearly $180 million combined.
Finisar ( FNSR ) and Acacia Communications ( ACIA ) also sell optical devices to Huawei.
Huawei Flap Follows ZTE Sanctions Canadian authorities on Wednesday arrested Huawei chief financial officer Meng Wanzhou at the request of the U.S. Huawei has been under investigation for potential violations of U.S. trade sanctions on Iran. The U.S. is seeking her extradition.
The Huawei sell-off is similar to the one that followed U.S. sanctions imposed on ZTE in April. It's the No. 2 maker of telecom network gear in China, behind Huawei.
The U.S. ultimately lifted sanctions on ZTE in June after the gear maker agreed to pay a fine and make management changes.
Huawei An Apple Smartphone Rival Aside from the Iran-related probes, the Trump administration has been pressuring other countries to bar Huawei gear from their telecom networks because of concerns over espionage.
In addition to making network gear, Huawei makes smartphones. It's a rival of Apple ( AAPL ) in the smartphone market.
Lumentum sells 3D sensor devices to Apple for iPhones. Apple uses the 3D sensors in facial recognition to unlock screens.
Lumentum stock is down 40% from March, as new iPhone sales have disappointed. Lumentum stock fell in November when it lowered revenue guidance.
